correctness.rationale: At the antipodal point the two self-weights are exactly 3/4 and 7/8, yielding positive radial gain 9/4. All attention score derivatives vanish on six tangent directions. Exact tangent Jacobian consists of (2/9)[[1,1],[1,1]] and two copies of (4/9)I2; spectrum has five copies 4/9 plus zero, giving local exponential attraction by a strict contraction. Each isolated head fixes the antipodal configuration but has a symmetric second-coordinate multiplier 10/3 respectively -12/7, proving instability. Since I-D F is invertible, an attracting fixed point persists under sufficiently small smooth parameter perturbations. Direct independent numerical Jacobian/trajectory cross-checks pass; the universal local theorem relies on the exact proof.

value.rationale: The primary source identifies stable multihead bipartite points as unobserved; a construction with two individually unstable heads but a rigorously attracting joint antipodal pair supplies a structurally motivated positive answer, not a routine table lookup. The proof explains the mechanism: cancellation of opposite transverse value directions under distinct softmax weights with a common positive radial gain. Exact whole-spectrum control and local persistence turn a single numerical example into a reproducible robust dynamical witness; global attraction is not claimed.
